# PermissionDiff 0.1.1

A correctness and hardening patch. No new product features; existing behavior and interfaces are
unchanged except where noted below.

## Fixed

- **Custom invariants can no longer fake success.** A custom invariant runs in the parent process;
  if it terminated the process (for example `SystemExit(0)`), PermissionDiff could exit with a
  success code and report an incomplete evaluation as a pass. Custom-invariant termination,
  crashes, and invalid return values are now explicit evaluation errors (exit `3`). PermissionDiff
  never fails open.
- **Worker result channel is protected for the whole process lifetime.** Authorizer output written
  to stdout during interpreter shutdown (`atexit`) could corrupt the JSON result and turn a valid
  decision into an error. The worker now writes results on a private descriptor and keeps stdout
  redirected to stderr for the entire process, so `print`, raw `os.write`, import-time, and
  shutdown output can never contaminate the protocol.

## Hardened

- Restored dependency review as a blocking pull-request gate now that the repository dependency
  graph is active.
- Added security-critical regression tests for custom-invariant termination/return handling and
  late-lifetime worker stdout.

## Install

```bash
pip install permissiondiff==0.1.1
```

Python 3.12, 3.13, and 3.14 are supported.

## Security note (unchanged)

PermissionDiff evaluates trusted Python authorization code in a timeout-controlled subprocess,
which provides fault isolation, not a hostile-code security sandbox. Run it in an isolated
development or CI environment and never connect test authorizers to production systems, secrets, or
side effects. Reproducible findings require deterministic authorizers and matching package, Python,
configuration, seed, and corpus inputs.

See the [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/abishekgiri/permissiondiff/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) for
details.
